episode_title: Beyond the Business: Building a Brand That Stands Out with Amie Seier - Episode 102

real_qa.q: What was Amie Seier's career progression before opening The Community Gym?
real_qa.r: Amie earned a degree in communications from Creative Communications in Winnipeg and started her career in 2012 as a social media manager posting on Facebook for brands. She progressed to work for national clothing brands, tourism bodies, and creative agencies before becoming head of digital marketing for Cabela's Canada. She was also the first employee at Flair Airlines when it launched, which gave her confidence that she could open her own business.
real_qa.requete: Amie Seier career before Community Gym

real_qa.q: How did The Community Gym survive the COVID-19 pandemic shutdown in 2020?
real_qa.r: The Community Gym opened in May 2019 and shut down nine months later when the pandemic hit. Amy immediately created a formal video message to communicate honestly with members. She drew on her public relations and communications background to pivot quickly to online classes and on-demand programming to keep people moving and connected during lockdown.
real_qa.requete: Community Gym COVID-19 pandemic shutdown response

real_qa.q: Why did Amie Seier leave her corporate job to start The Community Gym?
real_qa.r: After taking a spin class in Calgary, Amie felt called to create a fitness space that offered more than just a workout. When she returned to Winnipeg, the existing spin studios did not capture the essence of what she had experienced in Calgary. She quit her corporate job and invested all her savings because she felt the call was too loud not to listen to, despite initially not wanting to own a small business.
real_qa.requete: why Amie Seier quit corporate job gym

real_qa.q: What marketing and branding philosophy does Amie Seier apply to The Community Gym?
real_qa.r: Amie believes in showing, not telling when it comes to brand values like empowerment and inclusivity. She applies the principle that brand is the outside of your house while culture is the inside, and both must be aligned. Rather than stating values on walls, she lives them through hiring practices, creative content, and community engagement, trusting that people will see and respond to authentic action.

real_qa.q: How many members has The Community Gym served according to Amie Seier?
real_qa.r: In 2023 alone, The Community Gym had 3,000 people through its doors. Amie reflects on the ripple effect of this impact, noting that even if just a fraction of those members had their lives changed for the better—whether through fitness, community connection, or personal challenges like divorce—the business has achieved deep purpose.

guest.bio_context: Amy has a background in communications and marketing, having worked for national brands, Cabela's Canada as head of digital marketing, and as first employee at Flair Airlines. She discovered spin fitness in Calgary and launched The Community Gym through pop-up spin classes at the Forks in Winnipeg in May 2019, nine months before the COVID-19 pandemic forced gyms to close. During the pandemic, she rapidly pivoted to online classes and on-demand programming to keep members connected.

real_quote: If I can do that, make a living, help other people make a living and then change people's lives and do something that I created, like I figured it out. This feels like deeply satisfying for me.

Timeline to pandemic shutdown: nine months after May 2019 grand opening (February 2020)
Members served in 2023: 3,000 people through the doors
Year of personal epiphany during divorce vacation: 2023
Amie's first non-diverse hire: 2023 (did not hire a straight white guy until this year)
